title: Home & neighbourhood
goal: Rent a flat, sort out bills and maintenance, report what is broken and get the owner to fix it, and keep the peace with the neighbours.
intro:
Most young people in Hyderabad, Vijayawada or Vizag rent a **flat** in an apartment block, and life there runs on a handful of words: **ఓనర్** (the owner), **అడ్వాన్స్** (the deposit), **మెయింటెనెన్స్**, **కరెంటు బిల్లు** and the all-important **వాచ్‌మెన్**. This unit gives you that vocabulary, almost all of it English said the Telugu way.

The grammar is about **complaining well**. First you say what's wrong (*నీళ్ళు రావట్లేదు*, the water isn't coming; *తలుపు విరిగిపోయింది*, the door has broken), then you ask: gently (*... చేయిస్తే బాగుంటుంది*, it'd be good if you got it done), politely (*... తగ్గించగలరా?*, could you turn it down?) and, if it comes to that, firmly (*... చేయించాల్సిందే*, it has to be done). Finally, the **causative** from Unit 25 comes back for the jobs owners have done: *ప్లంబరుని పిలిపిస్తాను* (I'll get the plumber called in).

grammar.title: Saying what's wrong: -ట్లేదు, -తోంది and -ఇపోయింది
grammar.body:
A good complaint says **what is happening**, not just what happened once. Telugu has three verb shapes for this, and you met all of them earlier; here they come together.

**1. Something keeps not happening: -ట్లేదు.** The present continuous negative is written as the verbal noun + లేదు (*రావడం లేదు*, 'is not coming'). In speech it shrinks to **-ట్లేదు** (or -టం లేదు):
రా → **రావట్లేదు** (isn't coming) · పని చేయు → **పని చేయట్లేదు** (isn't working) · తిరుగు → **తిరగట్లేదు** (isn't turning) · వెలుగు → **వెలగట్లేదు** (isn't lighting up) · ఎత్తు → **ఎత్తట్లేదు** (isn't picking up)
The stem is the one you use before -ండి: రా**వ**ండి → రావట్లేదు, తిర**గ**ండి → తిరగట్లేదు.

**2. Something keeps happening: -తోంది.** The spoken present continuous (written -తున్నది): *లీక్ అవుతోంది* (it's leaking), *గోల చేస్తున్నారు* (they're making a racket).

**3. Something has broken or run out: past stem + పోయింది.** పోవు ('go') after the -ఇ form adds 'and it's gone / for good': *విరిగిపోయింది* (it's broken), *పాడైపోయింది* (it's stopped working), *ఆగిపోయింది* (it's stopped), *అయిపోయింది* (it's run out).

**Since when** goes in front with **నుంచి**: *మూడు రోజుల నుంచి*, *నిన్న రాత్రి నుంచి*.

**The trap**: *నీళ్ళు రాలేదు* means 'the water didn't come' (one time, today). For a problem that is still going on, say *నీళ్ళు రావట్లేదు*. And *రాదు* means 'it doesn't come (ever)', which sounds like you're describing the building, not complaining.

examples.native: మూడు రోజుల నుంచి నీళ్ళు సరిగ్గా రావట్లేదు.
examples.roman: mūḍu rōjula nunchi nīḷḷu sariggā rāvaṭlēdu.
examples.en: The water hasn't been coming properly for three days.

When I call, the owner doesn't pick up.

grammar.title: Asking nicely, then firmly
grammar.body:
Telugu speakers almost never open a complaint with a bare command. Climb this ladder, and only go up a step when you need to.

**1. Hint: -తే బాగుంటుంది** ('it would be good if...'). Conditional (Unit 19) + బాగుంటుంది: *ఈ వారంలో చేయిస్తే బాగుంటుంది* (it'd be good if you got it done this week). Negative: -కపోతే బాగుంటుంది, *పెట్టకపోతే బాగుంటుంది* (it'd be nice if you didn't park there). This is the most polite way to tell a neighbour off.

**2. Ask: -తారా? / -గలరా?** 'Will you...?' is the non-past question: *తగ్గిస్తారా?* 'Could you...?' adds **-గల-** (can, Unit 15): *తగ్గించగలరా?* Add **కొంచెం** (a little) and **ఒకసారి** (once, just) to soften: *ఒకసారి వచ్చి చూస్తారా?* (could you just come and have a look?)

**3. Polite command: -ండి**, with దయచేసి or ప్లీజ్ if you are annoyed: *దయచేసి గోల చేయకండి*.

**4. Insist: -ఆల్సిందే** ('it simply has to be'). Take the must-form -ఆలి, turn it into -ఆల్సింది and add emphatic -ఏ: చేయాలి → **చేయాల్సిందే**, చెప్పాలి → **చెప్పాల్సిందే**. Back it up with an 'otherwise' in -కపోతే: *మీరు చేయించకపోతే నేనే చేయిస్తాను* (if you don't, I'll get it done myself).

**The trap**: *ఇవ్వండి* or *తగ్గించండి* to an older neighbour or the owner sounds like an order. Wrap it as a question, *ఇస్తారా? తగ్గిస్తారా?*, and use అంకుల్ / ఆంటీ / గారు.

examples.native: ఈ వారంలో బాగు చేయిస్తే బాగుంటుంది అంకుల్.
examples.roman: ī vāramlō bāgu chēyistē bāguṇṭundi aṅkul.
examples.en: It would be good if you could get it fixed this week, uncle.

examples.native: రాత్రి పది తర్వాత కొంచెం సౌండ్ తగ్గించగలరా?

examples.en: Could you keep the volume down a bit after ten at night?

grammar.title: Causatives revisited: getting the owner to get it done
grammar.body:
Unit 25 taught the causative **-ఇంచు**: *చేయించు* (get done), *కుట్టించు* (get stitched). At home you use it all the time, because the tenant asks, the owner arranges and a plumber or electrician does the work.

**The forms you need with an owner**
• *చేయిస్తారా? / ఎప్పుడు చేయిస్తారు?* (will you get it done? when?)
• *చేయించాలి* (it needs to be got done) · *చేయించాల్సిందే* (it must be)
• **-ఇంచి ఇవ్వు**, done *for* you (Unit 25): *బాగు చేయించి ఇవ్వండి* (please get it fixed for me)
• the owner's answer: *చేయిస్తాను*, or, a week later, *చేయించాను* (I got it done)

**Whom you get to do it** takes **-తో** (or **చేత**, more careful): *ప్లంబరుతో చేయించాను* (I had the plumber do it). The person you *send for* takes -ని: *ఎలక్ట్రీషియన్‌ని పిలిపిస్తాను*.

**A few irregular ones worth knowing**: పిలుచు (call) → **పిలిపించు** (get someone called in, send for) · తెచ్చు (bring) → **తెప్పించు** (have brought, order in) · మార్చు → **మార్పించు** · పెట్టు → **పెట్టించు** (get put in, installed). Loanword verbs just change the helper: పెయింట్ వేయు → **పెయింట్ వేయించు**.

**The trap** is the same as in Unit 25, and the owner will love it if you get it wrong: *మీరు బాగు చేశారా?* asks whether he fixed it with his own hands.

culture: Flat-hunting in Hyderabad starts with the **To-Let** boards hung on gates and a chat with the watchman; these days also with apps and WhatsApp groups. Expect an **advance** (deposit) of two or three months' rent and an eleven-month agreement. Many owners say *ఫ్యామిలీకి మాత్రమే* (families only), and some want vegetarian tenants; *బ్యాచిలర్స్* often end up in shared flats. Tenants usually call the owner **అంకుల్ / ఆంటీ** or **ఓనర్ గారు**, and owners call young tenants **అమ్మా / బాబూ** with *నువ్వు*: warm, but it also tells you who is in charge. Complaints go through gently, often via the watchman or the apartment WhatsApp group, and a direct *ఇది తప్పు* to an older neighbour is a last resort; *-తే బాగుంటుంది* does the job with no loss of face. Water is the great Hyderabad topic: in summer blocks rely on tankers and the watchman switches the motor on and off at set hours. Neighbours bring sweets at Sankranti or after a family wedding, and *ఏదైనా అవసరమైతే అడగండి* is meant: people really do borrow milk, keys and phone chargers.

tip.title: Asking about a flat
tip.body:
- **అద్దెకి** = for rent: *ఫ్లాట్ అద్దెకి ఉందా?*
- Prices need no verb: **అద్దె ఎంత? అడ్వాన్స్ ఎంత?**
- Most flat words are English said the Telugu way: ఫ్లాట్, అడ్వాన్స్ (deposit), అగ్రిమెంట్, పార్కింగ్.
- Call the owner **ఓనర్ గారు**, or అంకుల్ / ఆంటీ.

You can pay the bill right on your phone.
The watchman has the key.
If anyone comes, the watchman calls.
The lift only goes up to the fifth floor.
The garbage van comes every morning.

tip.title: What's wrong: -ట్లేదు and -ఇపోయింది
tip.body:
- Keeps **not** happening: **-ట్లేదు** (careful -డం లేదు): నీళ్ళు **రావట్లేదు**, గీజర్ పని **చేయట్లేదు**.
- Keeps happening: **-తోంది**: లీక్ **అవుతోంది**.
- Has broken / run out: **-ఇపోయింది**: **విరిగిపోయింది**, **అయిపోయింది**.
- Trap: *రాలేదు* = didn't come (once). For an ongoing problem say *రావట్లేదు*.

sentences.native: గీజర్ పని చేయట్లేదు, వేడి నీళ్ళు రావట్లేదు.
sentences.roman: gījar pani chēyaṭlēdu, vēḍi nīḷḷu rāvaṭlēdu.
sentences.en: The geyser isn't working, there's no hot water.
The tap has been leaking all night.
The balcony door has broken.

sentences.native: కుళాయిలో నీళ్ళు రావట్లేదు, ట్యాంక్ ఖాళీ అయిపోయిందేమో.
sentences.roman: kuḷāyilō nīḷḷu rāvaṭlēdu, ṭyāṅk khāḷī ayipōyindēmō.
sentences.en: No water's coming from the tap; maybe the tank has run dry.
The lift hasn't been working for a week.
The chair leg has snapped.
Oh no, the power's gone again!
I keep calling the owner, he isn't picking up.
There are far too many mosquitoes in the house.
There are cockroaches running around the kitchen!

lessons.title: Getting the owner to fix it

tip.title: Get it done: -ఇంచు again
tip.body:
- To the owner: **చేయిస్తారా?** (will you get it done?) · **చేయించి ఇవ్వండి** (get it done for me).
- Who does the work takes **-తో**: ప్లంబరు**తో** చేయించాను.
- Send for someone: పిలుచు → **పిలిపించు**; bring → **తెప్పించు**; put in → **పెట్టించు**.
- Trap: *మీరు బాగు చేశారా?* = did you fix it with your own hands?

sentences.native: ఓనర్ గారు, గీజర్ ఎప్పుడు రిపేర్ చేయిస్తారు?
sentences.roman: ōnar gāru, gījar eppuḍu ripēr chēyistāru?
sentences.en: When will you get the geyser repaired, sir?
I'll send the plumber tomorrow morning.

sentences.native: నేను నిన్న ఎలక్ట్రీషియన్‌తో ఫ్యాను బాగు చేయించాను.
sentences.roman: nēnu ninna elakṭrīṣiyantō phyānu bāgu chēyinchānu.
sentences.en: I had an electrician fix the fan yesterday.

sentences.native: ట్యాంక్ శుభ్రం చేయించాలి, నీళ్ళు మురికిగా వస్తున్నాయి.
sentences.roman: ṭyāṅk shubhram chēyinchāli, nīḷḷu murikigā vastunnāyi.
sentences.en: The tank needs cleaning, the water is coming out dirty.

sentences.native: గోడలకి చెమ్మ వచ్చింది, మళ్ళీ పెయింట్ వేయించాలి.
sentences.roman: gōḍalaki chemma vachchindi, maḷḷī peyiṇṭ vēyinchāli.
sentences.en: The walls have gone damp, they need repainting.

sentences.native: ఓనర్ పాత పైపు తీయించి కొత్తది పెట్టించారు.
sentences.roman: ōnar pāta paipu tīyinchi kottadi peṭṭinchāru.
sentences.en: The owner had the old pipe taken out and a new one put in.
Get an electrician in and show him the geyser.

sentences.native: మీరే ప్లంబరుతో చేయించి బిల్లు నాకు పంపండి.
sentences.roman: mīrē plambarutō chēyinchi billu nāku pampaṇḍi.
sentences.en: Get the plumber to do it yourself and send me the bill.
Don't worry, I'll take care of it.
Take the cost of this repair off the rent.

lessons.title: Keeping the peace with the neighbours

tip.title: Asking nicely, then firmly
tip.body:
- Hint: **-తే బాగుంటుంది** (it'd be good if…): చెప్**తే బాగుంటుంది**.
- Ask: **-తారా?** / **-గలరా?** + కొంచెం: సౌండ్ **తగ్గించగలరా?**
- Command only with దయచేసి: **చేయకండి**.
- Insist: **-ఆల్సిందే**: చెప్పాల్సిందే (it simply has to be done).

sentences.en: The next-door neighbours are really nice.
Could you turn the volume down a little at night?

sentences.native: మీ టీవీ సౌండ్ కొంచెం తగ్గిస్తారా? పాప పడుకుంది.
sentences.roman: mī ṭīvī sauṇḍ konchem taggistārā? pāpa paḍukundi.
sentences.en: Could you turn your TV down a bit? The baby's asleep.
The kids are playing, please bear with it a bit.

sentences.native: మీ కారు మా పార్కింగ్‌లో పెట్టకపోతే బాగుంటుంది.
sentences.roman: mī kāru mā pārkiṅglō peṭṭakapōtē bāguṇṭundi.
sentences.en: It would be nice if you didn't park your car in our space.
It would be good to have a quiet word with them once.

sentences.native: దయచేసి రాత్రి పది తర్వాత గోల చేయకండి.
sentences.roman: dayachēsi rātri padi tarvāta gōla chēyakaṇḍi.
sentences.en: Please don't make noise after ten at night.
This is the third time; this time I've got to tell the owner.
Have you just moved into this flat?

sentences.native: ఏదైనా అవసరమైతే మా ఇంటికి రండి, మొహమాటం వద్దు.
sentences.roman: ēdainā avasaramaitē mā iṇṭiki raṇḍi, mohamāṭam vaddu.
sentences.en: If you need anything, come over to ours, don't be shy.

sentences.native: మేము ఆదివారం కొత్త ఇంటికి షిఫ్ట్ అవుతున్నాం.
sentences.roman: mēmu ādivāram kotta iṇṭiki shiphṭ avutunnām.
sentences.en: We're moving to the new place on Sunday.

sentences.native: కొత్త ఫ్లాట్ ఆఫీసుకి దగ్గర, అందుకే షిఫ్ట్ అవుతున్నాం.
sentences.roman: kotta phlāṭ āphīsuki daggara, andukē shiphṭ avutunnām.
sentences.en: The new flat is near the office, that's why we're moving.

sentences.native: ఖాళీ చేసే ముందు ఓనర్‌కి ఒక నెల ముందే చెప్పాలి.
sentences.roman: khāḷī chēsē mundu ōnarki oka nela mundē cheppāli.
sentences.en: Before you move out you have to tell the owner a month ahead.
We'll move out at the end of this month.
Have you packed all your things?

sentences.native: షిఫ్ట్ అయ్యే ముందు ఇల్లు శుభ్రం చేయించాలి.
sentences.roman: shiphṭ ayyē mundu illu shubhram chēyinchāli.
sentences.en: We need to get the house cleaned before we move.
If anything gets broken, they take it out of the deposit.
The owner still hasn't given the deposit back.
No mosquitoes in the new place, phew!
